{{Short description|Inequality in probability theory}}
{{one source |date=March 2024}}
In [[probability theory]], '''Hoeffding's lemma''' is an [[inequality (mathematics)|inequality]] that bounds the [[moment-generating function]] of any [[bounded function|bounded]] [[random variable]],<ref>{{cite book|author=Pascal Massart|title=Concentration Inequalities and Model Selection: Ecole d'Eté de Probabilités de Saint-Flour XXXIII - 2003|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZI67BQAAQBAJ&pg=PA21|date=26 April 2007|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-3-540-48503-2|page=21}}</ref> implying that such variables are [[Sub-Gaussian distribution|subgaussian]]. It is named after the [[Finnish people|Finnish]]&ndash;[[United States|American]] [[mathematical statistics|mathematical statistician]] [[Wassily Hoeffding]].

The proof of Hoeffding's lemma uses [[Taylor's theorem]].  Hoeffding's lemma is itself used in the proof of [[Hoeffding's inequality]] as well as the generalization [[McDiarmid's inequality]].

==Statement==

Let ''X'' be any real-valued random variable such that <math>a \leq X \leq b</math> [[almost surely]], i.e. with probability one.  Then, for all <math> \lambda \in \mathbb{R}</math>,

:<math>\mathbb{E} \left[ e^{\lambda X} \right] \leq \exp \Big(\lambda\mathbb{E}[X]+ \frac{\lambda^2 (b - a)^2}{8} \Big),</math>

or equivalently,

:<math>\mathbb{E} \left[ e^{\lambda (X - \mathbb{E}[X])} \right] \leq \exp \Big(\frac{\lambda^2 (b - a)^2}{8} \Big).</math>

===Proof===
The following proof is direct but somewhat ad-hoc.

{{Math proof|title=Proof|proof= 
Let <math>\mu = \mathbb{E}[X]</math>. Since the conclusion involves <math>b-a</math>, without loss of generality, one may replace <math>X</math> by <math>X - \mu</math>, <math>a</math> by <math>a - \mu</math>, and <math>b</math> by <math>b - \mu</math>, which leaves the difference <math>b-a</math> unchanged, and assume <math>\mathbb{E}[X] = 0</math>, so that <math>a \leq 0 \leq b</math>.

Since <math> e^{\lambda x}</math> is a convex function of <math>x</math>, we have that for all <math>x \in [a,b]</math>,

:<math>e^{\lambda x}\leq \frac{b-x}{b-a}e^{\lambda a}+\frac{x-a}{b-a}e^{\lambda b}</math>

So, 
:<math>\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}\left[e^{\lambda X}\right] &\leq \frac{b-\mathbb{E}[X]}{b-a}e^{\lambda a}+\frac{\mathbb{E}[X]-a}{b-a}e^{\lambda b}\\
&=  \frac{b}{b-a}e^{\lambda a} + \frac{-a}{b-a}e^{\lambda b} \\
&= e^{L(\lambda(b-a))},
\end{align}
</math>

where <math> L(h)= \frac{ha}{b-a}+\ln(1 + \frac{a - e^ha}{b-a})</math>. By computing derivatives, we find

:<math> L(0)=L'(0)=0</math> and <math>L''(h)= -\frac{ab e^h}{(b-a e^h)^2}</math>.

From the [[Inequality of arithmetic and geometric means|AMGM]] inequality we thus see that <math>L''(h)\le\frac14</math> for all <math>h</math>, and thus, from [[Taylor's theorem]], there is some <math>0 \le \theta \le 1</math> such that

:<math> L(h) = L(0) + h L'(0) + \frac{1}{2} h^2 L''(h\theta) \leq \frac{1}{8}h^2.</math>

Thus, <math> \mathbb{E}\left[e^{\lambda X}\right] \leq e^{\frac{1}{8}\lambda^2(b-a)^2}</math>.
}}

==Statement==

This statement and proof uses the language of [[Sub-Gaussian distribution|subgaussian]] variables and [[exponential tilting]], and is less ad-hoc.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Boucheron |first1=Stéphane |last2=Lugosi |first2=Gábor |last3=Massart |first3=Pascal |title=Concentration Inequalities: A Nonasymptotic Theory of Independence |date=2013 |publisher=Oxford University Press}}</ref>{{rp|Lemma 2.2}}

Let <math>X</math> be any real-valued random variable such that <math>a \leq X \leq b</math> [[almost surely]], i.e. with probability one. Then it is subgaussian with [[Sub-Gaussian distribution#Variance proxy|variance proxy]] norm <math>\|X\|_{vp} \leq \frac{b-a}{2}</math>.

{{Math proof|title=Proof|proof= 

By the definition of variance proxy, it suffices to show that its cumulant generating function <math>K(t) := \log E[e^{t(X-E[X])}] </math> satisfies <math>K''(t) \leq (b-a)^2/4</math>. Explicit calculation shows <math display="block">K''(t) = \frac{E[(X-E[X])^2 e^{t(X-E[X])}]}{E[e^{t(X-E[X])}]} - \left(\frac{E[(X-E[X]) e^{t(X-E[X])}]}{E[e^{t(X-E[X])}]}\right)^2</math>Notice that the quantity <math>\frac{E[(X-E[X]) e^{t(X-E[X])}]}{E[e^{t(X-E[X])}]} = E\left[(X-E[X])\frac{e^{t(X-E[X])}}{E[e^{t(X-E[X])}]} \right] </math> is precisely the expectation of a random variable obtained by exponentially tilting <math>X - E[X] </math>. Let this variable be <math>Y_t </math>. It remains to bound <math>Var[Y_t] \leq (b-a)^2/4 </math>.

Notice that <math>Y_t </math> still has range <math>[a-E[X], b-E[X]] </math>. So translate it to <math>Z_t := Y_t - \frac{a+b - E[X]}{2}  </math> so that its range has midpoint zero. It remains to bound <math>Var[Z_t] \leq (b-a)^2/4 </math>. However, now the bound is trivial, since <math>|Z_t| \leq \frac{b-a}{2} </math>.
}}Given this general case, the formula <math>\mathbb{E} \left[ e^{\lambda (X - \mathbb{E}[X])} \right] \leq e^{\frac{\lambda^2 (b - a)^2}{8}}</math> is a mere corollary of a general property of variance proxy.
